question.text: Total number of moles of AgCl precipitated on addition of excess of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>AgNO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> to one mole each of the following complexes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mrow><mi>Co</mi><msub><mfenced><msub><mi>NH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mfenced><mn>4</mn></msub><msub><mi>Cl</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mfenced><mi>Cl</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mrow><mi>Ni</mi><msub><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow></mfenced><mn>6</mn></msub></mrow></mfenced><msub><mi>Cl</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mrow><mi>Pt</mi><msub><mfenced><msub><mi>NH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>Cl</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mrow><mi>Pd</mi><msub><mfenced><msub><mi>NH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mfenced><mn>4</mn></msub></mrow></mfenced><msub><mi>Cl</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> is

solution.text:
Silver nitrate on reaction of chloride ion gives silver chloride as precipitate. Chloride ions outside of coordination sphere will only give precipitates. Thus,
CoNH34Cl2Cl⇒ Gives 1 mole AgCl
NiH2O6Cl2⇒ Gives 2 moles AgCl
PtNH32Cl2⇒ Gives No AgCl
PdNH34Cl2⇒ Gives 2 moles AgCl
Total number of moles of AgCl=5 mole.
